t: Long ago, there was a woman named Naomi. Her husband and her two sons had died... and now only Ruth, her son's wife, was left with her.
m: Narrator | storyteller opening; soft and slow; a real pause before 'had died', the voice drops and goes tender, never gloomy | at most 14.6 s
d: Picture: bedtime, a big picture book open, the child leaning on you. (Ruth 1:1-5)

t: Ruth, my dear... I'm going home to Bethlehem. You're still young. Go back to your mother's house, all right?
m: Naomi | tired and loving, a little choked; a soft sigh before she starts; the last 'all right?' is gentle, almost begging | at most 9.1 s
d: Picture: you hold the hand of someone you love and tell her to leave you. (Ruth 1:8-9)

t: No, I won't leave you! Where you go, I will go. Where you stay, I will stay. Your God... will be my God.
m: Ruth | from the heart, close to tears but steady; quick and firm on 'No, I won't leave you', then slower and warmer; a breath before 'Your God' | at most 10.6 s
d: Picture: you hold your mother-in-law's hands tight and won't let go. (Ruth 1:16)

t: They walked and walked, a long, long way, and at last they came to Bethlehem. It was barley harvest time.
m: Narrator | a walking rhythm in the voice ('walked and walked'); brighter on 'at last'; a small smile on the harvest | at most 9.5 s
d: Picture: your finger walks along the long road in the picture book to Bethlehem. (Ruth 1:19, 1:22)

t: Oh... when I left, I had everything. Now I've come home... with nothing.
m: Naomi | a long sigh first; quiet, empty; slow, with a break before the second half | at most 8.3 s
d: Picture: you stand at the door of an empty old home. (Ruth 1:21)

t: Don't be sad, Mother. I'll go and pick up grain in the fields, then we'll have food to eat!
m: Ruth | gentle first, then bright and eager with a little smile; a bit quicker at the end | at most 5.3 s
d: Picture: you crouch by a sad grandmother and try to make her smile. (Ruth 2:2)

t: In Israel, the harvesters left some grain behind for poor people to pick up. So Ruth knelt at the edge of the field and picked it up, one stalk at a time.
m: Narrator | calm, explaining, like a parent pointing at a picture; slow on 'one stalk at a time' | at most 10.2 s
d: Picture: you point to the stalks at the edge of the field in the book. (Ruth 2:2-3; Leviticus 19:9-10)

t: The field belonged to a man named Boaz. He was rich, and he was very kind.
m: Narrator | warm, a little admiring | at most 7.0 s
d: Picture: you introduce a good man you admire. (Ruth 2:1, 2:3)

t: Good morning, everyone! The Lord be with you!
m: Boaz | hearty and friendly, loud enough to carry across a field; a big smile | at most 3.8 s
d: Picture: early morning, you walk into your field and call out to your workers. (Ruth 2:4)

t: The Lord bless you too!
m: Reapers | three or four workers answering together from across the field, cheerful, a little ragged | at most 2.5 s
d: Picture: you are bent over in the field and look up to call back to the owner. (Ruth 2:4)

t: Hm? Who's that young woman over there?
m: Boaz | he stops mid-step, curious and gentle; a thinking 'Hm' first | at most 2.5 s
d: Picture: you suddenly spot someone new and tilt your head. (Ruth 2:5)

t: Stay here and gather in my field. Don't go anywhere else. And when you're thirsty, go and drink from the water jars.
m: Boaz | kind, fatherly, unhurried; as if pointing at the jars on 'water jars' | at most 8.9 s
d: Picture: you tell a newcomer not to worry and to drink when thirsty. (Ruth 2:8-9)

t: I'm a stranger here... why are you so kind to me?
m: Ruth | shy, amazed, almost a whisper; the question rises gently | at most 4.9 s
d: Picture: a grown-up is very kind to you; you quietly ask why. (Ruth 2:10)

t: I've heard all about how good you've been to Naomi. May God reward you for it!
m: Boaz | warm and moved, a smile in the voice; the blessing a little slower | at most 6.5 s
d: Picture: you've heard how good someone has been, and you are glad for her. (Ruth 2:11-12)

t: Psst... when you cut the barley, drop a little extra on purpose... for her to pick up! Heh heh.
m: Boaz | stage whisper, playful, grinning; slow and secretive, then a cheeky lift on 'for her to pick up', then a little chuckle | at most 7.3 s
d: Picture: you secretly slip an extra sweet to a friend. (Ruth 2:15-16)

t: By evening, Ruth had gathered a great big bundle of barley!
m: Narrator | building delight; big and round on 'great big bundle' | at most 4.2 s
d: Picture: you show the child a huge armful: look how much! (Ruth 2:17)

t: Oh my! So much! Whose field were you working in today?
m: Naomi | genuinely amazed, the first time she sounds happy; a little laugh on 'So much!' | at most 8.3 s
d: Picture: a child brings home a huge armful and your eyes go wide. (Ruth 2:19)

t: A man called Boaz. He was so kind to me!
m: Ruth | happy, a bit breathless, proud | at most 3.0 s
d: Picture: you ran all the way home to tell good news. (Ruth 2:19)

t: Boaz? Why, he's family! Thank God... He hasn't forgotten us!
m: Naomi | surprise turning into joy and thankful tears; a catch in the voice before 'He hasn't forgotten us' | at most 9.0 s
d: Picture: you suddenly see you were cared for all along, and tears come. (Ruth 2:20)

t: Naomi thought, 'If only Boaz would take care of Ruth!' So one night, Ruth went to find Boaz at the threshing floor.
m: Narrator | hushed, night-time, a little secret and hopeful | at most 10.4 s
d: Picture: at night you whisper a secret plan to the child. (Ruth 3:1-6)

t: Boaz, you're part of our family... will you please take care of us?
m: Ruth | soft, nervous, brave; a small breath before 'will you please' | at most 6.4 s
d: Picture: you gather your courage to ask a grown-up for help. (Ruth 3:9)

t: Don't be afraid, my daughter. Everyone knows you're a good woman. I will take care of you, I promise!
m: Boaz | very gentle, then firm and sure on the promise; a smile | at most 7.2 s
d: Picture: a frightened child asks you for help and you reassure her. (Ruth 3:10-11)

t: And so Boaz married Ruth. The whole town came to celebrate with them!
m: Narrator | bright and happy, a smile you can hear | at most 4.9 s
d: Picture: you describe a joyful wedding. (Ruth 4:9-13)

t: Before long, they had a baby boy. They named him Obed.
m: Narrator | soft and tender, like looking into a cradle; slow on the name | at most 5.5 s
d: Picture: you lean over a sleeping baby in a cradle. (Ruth 4:13, 4:17)

t: My little grandson... God really didn't forget me!
m: Naomi | happy tears, half laughing; a rocking rhythm; the last words full of wonder | at most 5.9 s
d: Picture: you rock your newborn grandson in your arms. (Ruth 4:14-16)

t: And guess what? When Obed grew up, he had a grandson named David. Yes, the David who beat Goliath!
m: Narrator | playful, leaning in to share a secret; a big happy reveal on 'David' | at most 8.4 s
d: Picture: you lean to the child's ear: want to know a secret? (Ruth 4:17, 4:22)

t: Ruth never left Naomi, and God took care of them all along. You can love your family like that too!
m: Narrator | warm moral, speaking right to the child; a smile on the last sentence | at most 7.3 s
d: Picture: the story is over and you stroke the child's hair. (Ruth 1:16, 2:12)
